title: fix(kanban,calendar): surface write failures instead of silently swallowing them (cloud#864 A)
body:
## What

On a record surface, dragging a card into a different status column (Kanban) or
dragging an event to a new date (Calendar) issues a single-field `PATCH`. When
that write fails — most commonly a **row-level-security 403** (`code:
PERMISSION_DENIED`) — the drag handlers only `console.warn`/`console.error`'d
and snapped the item back, so the user saw **no feedback at all**: the status
just didn't change and nothing explained why.

This is part **(A)** of objectstack-ai/cloud#864 (the deterministic frontend bug).

## Changes

- **`@object-ui/react`**: new shared `extractWriteErrorMessage(err)` /
  `isPermissionError(err)` (`packages/react/src/utils/error-message.ts`). They
  normalise across both DataSource error shapes — the ObjectStack adapter's
  structured `.details`/`.message` and `ApiDataSource`'s JSON-tail-in-message —
  and strip `[Security] ` / `PERMISSION_DENIED:` prefixes.
- **`ObjectKanban.handleCardMove`** and **`ObjectCalendar.handleEventDropDefault`**:
  on failure, keep the optimistic revert but also `toast.error(...)` — a
  permission denial shows the already-localized `errors.unauthorized`
  ("You are not authorized to perform this action." / "您没有权限执行此操作。"),
  other errors show the server reason (fallback `table.saveFailed`).

## Note on the issue's scope

The issue also listed inline-edit and the edit form as silently swallowing. On
current `main` those already surface (inline `role="alert"` via
`InlineEditSaveBar`, and `toast.error` + inline error in the form). The genuine
silent swallows were the two drag surfaces, which is what this PR fixes. The
matching **ownership** fix (so a member can actually edit their app's seed data)
is option (B), handled in a separate cloud PR.

## Verification

- `type-check` clean for `@object-ui/react`, `@object-ui/plugin-kanban`,
  `@object-ui/plugin-calendar`.
- Existing kanban/calendar unit tests pass (the one failing suite,
  `plugin-calendar/src/registration.test.tsx`, fails identically on unmodified
  `main` — a pre-existing brittle non-spread mock of `@object-ui/react`).
